title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes and numbness in feet.

HPI
The patient presents today for a routine follow-up of their type 2 diabetes mellitus. They report ongoing sensation of tingling and occasional numbness in both feet. The patient has been stable on their current oral hypoglycemic regimen and reports consistent adherence. They deny any recent acute changes in symptoms or significant fluctuations in blood glucose levels.

Medication List
Metformin 500mg BID

Exam
General: Alert and oriented x3. In stable condition.
Extremities: Symmetrical sensation noted. Diminished sensation to light touch in bilateral toes. No active ulcers or skin breakdown observed.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Stable on current oral medication.
2. Peripheral neuropathy: The patient presents with symptoms of polyneuropathy. However, clinical evaluation suggests this condition is unrelated to diabetes.

Plan
Continue current dose of metformin. Patient advised to monitor for any new skin changes on feet. Follow up in 3 months for routine monitoring.
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code diabetes without complications and the polyneuropathy separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).
Long-term oral hypoglycemic use: add Z79.84.

distractors.why: Documentation of another cause overrides the 'with' presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
Z79.84 captures long-term oral hypoglycemic use.
